sources.citation: Birk, D. B. W. 1976. The MalakMalak language, Daly River (Western Arnhem Land). Pacific Linguistics B-45. Canberra: ANU. sec. 1.6 'The phonological word', pp. 15-17. DOI 10.15144/PL-B45
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: SISTER LANGUAGE (MalakMalak, mull1237) only: 'The phonological word in MalakMalak is a minimal utterance carrying one primary stress'; two word types -- stress on the first syllable and all odd-numbered syllables (2-,3-,4-,6-,8-syllable words), or on the second and all even-numbered syllables (5- and 7-syllable words, tetrasyllabic auxiliaries, mostly in the Verb Complex); 'Word stress carries little functional load'; primary stress accompanied by raised pitch. Mentions 'Dyeraity' only in the classification chart; says nothing about Tyeraity stress.
